greeting.speaker: Alder the Steward
text: You're armed, and you came in by the road instead of over the wall. That already puts you ahead of the last lot.
Armed, and walking slowly. I've learned to read both. Say your business.
Whatever you're selling, we bought it last spring and buried it by autumn. Talk anyway.

options.text: What happened to the last lot?
We're only passing through. Is there work?
Who speaks for this place when you're not standing in the road?
The well is dry and the fields are cut short. You're not going to last the winter.
Take this for the grain store. Don't make a speech about it.

again.speaker: Alder the Steward
text: You came back. Nobody comes back. I've had to think of something to say and I've not managed it.
Same road, same boots, fewer of you than I remember. Or more. I've stopped counting other people's.
The village saw you on the ridge and argued about whether to hope. You can settle it.

options.text: We said we'd bring the grain back. We've not forgotten.
Take this for the grain store. Don't make a speech about it.

the_last_lot.speaker: Alder the Steward
the_last_lot.text: Took the grain and the name of protectors with it. If you're the same, take it now and spare us the speech.

options.text: We're not. You'll have it back if we find it.

work.speaker: Alder the Steward
work.text: There's always work. Whether there's coin behind it is a different question — ask at the board and don't hold your breath.

read_the_village.speaker: Alder the Steward
read_the_village.text: ...No. We won't. You're the first one through here who bothered to look at us instead of past us.

misread.speaker: Alder the Steward
misread.text: We've lasted worse winters than you've seen summers. Move along.

held_to_it.speaker: Alder the Steward
held_to_it.text: Then I'll hold you to it, and so will everyone standing behind me.

cold.speaker: Alder the Steward
cold.text: I've stood aside for better and worse than you. Go on, then.

who_speaks.speaker: Alder the Steward
who_speaks.text: Nobody. There was a reeve, and there was a lord above him, and both of them are a rumour now. So it's me, in the road, arguing with strangers.

how_it_fares.speaker: Alder the Steward
text: Two fewer roofs and one more grave. That's a quiet month, by our reckoning.
The children have started playing at being you. I've not decided whether to stop them.
We ate. Nobody left in the night. I'll take it and not ask for more.

the_promise.speaker: Alder the Steward
the_promise.text: I know. I've had it repeated to me by every man who saw you say it. Bring it or don't, but come back and say which.

the_gift.speaker: Alder the Steward
the_gift.text: ...Then I won't make one. It'll be in the store by dark and nobody will be told whose it was.
